location: Note footnote 1 (Section 4, tex line 118), from 'so they are homotopic rel endpoints there, hence isotopic in $D_4$, and $\Phi$ fixes $\bs$' to the end of the footnote
evidence:
I checked each step of the footnote.
- Deleting strand 1 gives an isotopy rel {p2,p3,p4}, so (β*)Φ ≃ β* rel endpoints in D∖{p2,p4}. Correct.
- The inclusion D∖(α∪{p4}) → D∖{p2,p4} is a π1-isomorphism of free groups of rank 2: the loop around α goes to the loop around p2, since p1 is not removed. Both surfaces are aspherical, so the rel-endpoint homotopy transfers. Correct.
- 'hence isotopic in D_4' is true but not justified. The standard 'homotopic arcs are isotopic' needs a homotopy whose interior avoids the marked points, and this homotopy may pass through p3. The step does hold here: every simple arc from p* to p3 in D∖(α∪{p4}) is P_η(β*) for some push P_η of p3, and P_η(β*) ≃ β*·η^{±1}. So homotopic implies η = 1, which implies isotopic. That needs a Birman-exact-sequence argument the footnote does not give, and a careful reader is likely to flag it.
- The step is also unnecessary. Since α contains p1 and p2, D∖(α∪{p4}) ⊂ D∖{p1,p2,p4}, so the homotopy already lives where the push argument needs it. Φ = Push(δ) with δ in π1(D∖{p1,p2,p4},p3) takes β* to an arc homotopic there to β*·δ^{±1}.

One correction to the reviewer's replacement: 'Φ=1 because the push map is injective' is a non sequitur. A null-homotopic δ gives Φ = Push(δ) = Push(1) = 1 without injectivity.

The patched copy compiles.

But the finding overstates the problem, and one sentence of its replacement is something the authors could fairly object to. (a) 'The paper fixes no matrix convention for rho_n' ignores layout 124-125. There, Section 2 of the paper refers to [BB05, Section 4.2] for Burau's matrices. BB05 (arXiv math/0409205v2, PDF p. 46, checked on the rendered page) uses exactly the note's U. Its reduced form, with rows (1,-t,0), (0,-t,0), (0,-1,1) and -t at (i,i), equals diag(1,-1,1,..) R^T diag(1,-1,1,..) for every s_i^{+-1} with n = 3, 4, 5 (bb05_check.out). In that reduced form Phi0 = I at -1 and != I at 2, 1/2, 3 and 1/3, the identity holds with 1 + t^3, and Delta_3^2 maps to t^3 I_2. So the note's conventions are those of a survey written by two of the three authors. Saying so is fairer and more persuasive than saying the paper fixes no convention. (b) The PDF does give U explicitly, so an author can tell which convention the U and UT numbers use. Only the reduced form is missing. (c) The Fox statement is correct. My per-letter Fox Jacobians reproduce U exactly on Phi0. The chain rule J(uv) = J(u)J(v) holds on 40 random words for both half-twist directions and for both t and 1/t, and Fox of the other half twist gives U(mirror) (conv_check.out lines 1-5). Under the first 100 letters of Phi0, the images of x_1, ..., x_4 already have 0.7 to 2.9 million letters, so a whole-word Fox check of Phi0 is impossible. The letter-by-letter check in the reviewer's proposed script is the right approach. (d) 'Up to conjugation' also holds for R: at t0 = 5/3, for n = 4 and 5, there is an invertible C, unique up to scalar, with C R(s_i)(1/t0) = R(s_i^-1)(t0) C for all i. The depth is exactly 1 in both orientations (depth_check.out).
required_change: Replace tex line 152, through 'In each of these conventions:', with: All computations are exact, over $\mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm1}]$ or $\mathbb{Q}$. We used $\sigma_i\mapsto I_{i-1}\oplus\begin{pmatrix}1-t&t\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\oplus I_{n-i-1}$, the matrices of \cite[Section 4.2]{BB05}, to which Section 2 of \cite{BBB} refers for Burau's original definition. By Fox calculus these are the matrices of the action on $H$ in the basis of lifts of $x_1,\dots,x_n$, with $t$ the deck transformation corresponding to each $x_k$, when $\sigma_i$ acts by $x_i\mapsto x_ix_{i+1}x_i^{-1}$, $x_{i+1}\mapsto x_i$. We also used the transposed matrices, the reduced representation in which $\sigma_i$ replaces row $i$ of $I_{n-1}$ by $(t,-t,1)$ in columns $i-1,i,i+1$, and its transpose; conjugating this transpose by $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,1,\dots)$ gives the reduced matrices of \cite[Section 4.2]{BB05}. Replacing every $\sigma_i$ by the opposite half twist, or $t$ by $t^{-1}$, changes all of these by $t\mapsto t^{-1}$ up to conjugation. This does not affect statements at $t=-1$ or about depth, and for the other evaluations we also use $t=1/2$ and $t=1/3$. Triviality is checked with the Artin action of $\B_n$ on the free group $F_n$, and $f$ is $\sigma_i\mapsto\sigma_i$. In each of these conventions: The sentence beginning 'By Fox calculus' is optional. The rest is needed so that bullets 2 and 4 are well defined. Add to the bibliography, before [BBB26]: \bibitem[BB05]{BB05} J. S. Birman and T. E. Brendle, \emph{Braids: a survey}, in \emph{Handbook of Knot Theory}, Elsevier, Amsterdam, 2005, 19--103.
